chunks: And by this chain, from Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
was asked about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'The Most Merciful rose above the Throne' [Quran 20:5]
So he said: 'He is equal in relation to every thing; there is nothing closer to Him than another thing.'

key_terms.أَقْرَبَ: Closer — used comparatively to emphasize that God has no spatial proximity differences
key_terms.اسْتَوَى: Rose above/is even — interpreted as divine equidistance and omnipresence, not physical elevation
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne — the highest created realm, symbolizing divine sovereignty

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'The Most Merciful rose above the Throne' (Quran 20:5)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to explain the Quranic verse 'The Most Merciful rose above (istawa) the Throne' (Quran 20:5). He interpreted 'istawa' (rose above/is even) as meaning divine equality and equidistance from all things — God is not in a localized physical position above the Throne, but equally present to and equidistant from all of creation. This is a classic Shia theological response that refutes anthropomorphic interpretations, affirming God's transcendence and omnipresence.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Sahl, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Muhamad Bin Marid, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
was asked about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[20:5] The Beneficent is Even upon the Throne.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Even from everything. So there isn’t anything closer to Him<sup>azwj</sup> than a (another) thing’.
en.sarwar: 7. Sahl through the same chain of narrators has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Maridin the following. “A person asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah about the words of Allah, “The Beneficent God is dominant over the Throne (of the realm) [20:5].”
The Imam said, “He established His control in all things.
